definitions.explanation: A feeling of shyness or embarrassment when receiving praise, compliments, or attention. Not embarrassment from a mistake, but rather the awkward, bashful feeling of being in the spotlight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{褒|ほ}められて→褒める：01204_homeru⟧{面映|おもは}ゆい。
⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{表彰|ひょうしょう}→表彰：17400_hyoushou⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{面映|おもは}ゆかった。
examples.english: It was embarrassing to be honored in front of everyone.

examples.japanese: ⟦{久|ひさ}しぶり→久しぶり：01711_hisashiburi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「⟦ありがとう→ありがとう：00917_arigatou⟧」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}う→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、なんだ⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧{面映|おもは}ゆい{気持|きも}ちだった。
examples.english: Saying 'thank you' to my family after so long somehow felt self-conscious.

notes:
い-adjective:
- {面映|おもは}ゆい (present)
- {面映|おもは}ゆく⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (negative)
- {面映|おもは}ゆかった (past)
- {面映|おもは}ゆさ (noun form)

USAGE:
This is not the embarrassment of making a mistake or being caught doing something wrong. Rather, it describes the pleasant but uncomfortable feeling of modesty when receiving attention, praise, or affection — a mix of happiness and shyness.

REGISTER:
Somewhat literary and elegant. In casual speech, ⟦{恥|は}ずかしい→恥ずかしい：00843_hazukashii⟧ or ⟦{照|て}れ→照れる：08152_tereru⟧くさい are more common alternatives for similar feelings.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{照|て}れ→照れる：08152_tereru⟧くさい: awkward/embarrassed (from shyness) — more colloquial
- ⟦{恥|は}ずかしい→恥ずかしい：00843_hazukashii⟧: embarrassed/ashamed — broader meaning, includes shame
- きまり⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧: to feel awkward — focuses on social discomfort
